welcome.title: Build the product, not the foundation
welcome.subtitle: A production-minded Ionic React and Capacitor starter with strict architecture, accessible components, multilingual routes, and release gates already wired.
welcome.eyebrow: A serious starter for ambitious teams
welcome.trustIntro: Designed around proven open-source tools—not invented customer endorsements.

marketing.aboutIntro: Capacitor Ranger turns architectural decisions into visible modules, executable rules, and short context maps so a new contributor can become productive without reverse-engineering the repository.
marketing.aboutArchitectureBody: Imports flow in one direction, vendors have one owner, and feature modules expose deliberate public surfaces. Independent gates enforce the same shape reviewers expect.
marketing.aboutDeliveryBody: Authentication, typed API boundaries, testing fixtures, native synchronization, and release checks are ready to extend rather than rediscover.
marketing.aboutStandardsBody: Every hard rule names its reason, enforcement mechanism, and valid pattern. Teams can improve the system without turning it into folklore.
marketing.aboutOwnershipBody: Small files, explicit ownership, and one-hop documentation keep implementation details local while making system-level decisions easy to inspect.
marketing.featuresTitle: Everything needed to start with confidence
marketing.featuresIntro: The starter combines product-ready interaction patterns with unusually strict engineering feedback, without hiding the application behind a framework of custom abstractions.
marketing.featuresStrictBody: Type-aware ESLint, dual compiler checks, per-file coverage, architecture validation, dead-code detection, cycle checks, and copy parity fail loudly before review.
marketing.featuresNativeBody: Capacitor plugins are isolated behind typed owners, listeners capture cleanup handles, and Android/iOS synchronization is part of the release workflow.
marketing.featuresAiBody: Canonical rules, task skills, architecture maps, and generated context packs give coding agents the smallest relevant slice instead of the whole repository.
marketing.featuresExperienceBody: Navigation, breadcrumbs, cards, forms, loading states, theme controls, locale controls, and responsive layouts are shared primitives rather than page-local copies.
marketing.featuresOfflineBody: Installable PWA metadata, offline navigation fallback, deterministic mocks, accessible dark mode, and right-to-left layouts are first-class build outputs.
marketing.faqIntro: Clear answers about what the starter includes, where responsibility begins, and what still belongs to your product team.
marketing.faqStartQuestion: Can I start implementing a feature immediately?
marketing.faqStartAnswer: Yes. Copy an existing module anatomy, choose the matching skill, and run the focused gates. The starter already provides routing, state boundaries, forms, tests, and native wrappers.
marketing.faqBackendQuestion: Does the starter require a specific backend?
marketing.faqBackendAnswer: No. The HTTP boundary is designed for a NestJS-style API contract, but the schema-validated gateway and repository layers can target any JSON service.
marketing.faqNativeQuestion: Is a browser test the same as native verification?
marketing.faqNativeAnswer: No. Browser journeys validate the web application. Android requires Gradle and a device-quality pass; iOS compilation still requires macOS and Xcode.
marketing.faqCostQuestion: Does the AI documentation add runtime cost?
marketing.faqCostAnswer: No. Rules, skills, context maps, and generated agent packs are development assets. They are excluded from the shipped application bundle.
marketing.faqLocalesAnswer: Yes. Every supported language has a stable URL, visible translated copy, matching direction, self-referential canonical metadata, and alternate-language links.
marketing.contactIntro: Share the product goal, platform constraints, and where your current foundation slows the team down. The form prepares an email locally; it does not claim to send data to a backend.
marketing.contactSupportBody: Use the contact path for starter customization, migration planning, team conventions, and maintainability reviews.
marketing.contactResponseBody: After validation, you choose whether to open your mail application. Nothing is uploaded or silently submitted by this demo.
